editorial:
Ever wonder how one man could practically own an entire state? You get to see exactly how that happens in this movie about Huey P. Long. It follows his rise from a small-town lawyer to a powerful governor and senator in Louisiana during the Great Depression. The vibe is like a mix of a political thriller and a character study. You will see him use his charm and wit to help poor people while simultaneously breaking every rule in the book to keep his power. It is a wild ride that shows how a person can be a hero to some and a villain to others all at the same time.

What really makes this work is the acting, as the lead captures that loud, energetic personality perfectly. The pacing is quick, so you never feel bored while the political schemes unfold. A small downside is that it is an older TV movie, so some of the effects look dated. Still, if you love stories about power and corruption, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you are a movie buff, try to find the Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends on a tragic note. After spending years controlling Louisiana, Huey Long is finally cornered by his enemies. While he is walking through the halls of the State Capitol in Baton Rouge, a man named Carl Weiss shoots him. He dies from his wounds shortly after. The ending shows how his hunger for total power eventually led to his downfall, leaving behind a complicated legacy that people still argue about today.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves political power struggles and true history.
